result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a high-visibility continental crosswalk equipped with pedestrian signals and curb ramps. Wide, tree-lined sidewalks provide good separation from traffic, though the multi-lane roadway lacks a median refuge for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the full width of the roadway without a median refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the crosswalk

hazards.name: Roadway pavement degradation
hazards.description: Cracked and patched asphalt in the foreground may create uneven surfaces for those crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light to reduce turning conflicts.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with high-visibility crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. A significant construction site on the left side creates sidewalk obstructions and potential sightline issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Construction Obstruction
hazards.description: Orange barriers and construction materials block a portion of the sidewalk and roadway edge on the left side of the image.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and midground along the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction equipment and barriers may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk from the left.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the crosswalk entrance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers at the intersection.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light to increase visibility.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, visibility is significantly compromised by a large truck and parked vehicles near the crossing, and there are no visible traffic control devices like signals or stop signs.

hazards.name: Large vehicle visual obstruction
hazards.description: A large truck is stopped or parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, completely blocking the sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic from that direction.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, near the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Parked car visual obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection reduce the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to slow vehicle speeds and make pedestrians more prominent.

result.summary: The image depicts a high-density urban environment with significant pedestrian infrastructure, including wide sidewalks, a marked zebra crosswalk, and signalized control. However, the multi-lane one-way configuration and lack of a median refuge increase exposure for pedestrians crossing the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple travel lanes and a bike lane without a mid-crossing refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground zebra crosswalk across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Potential high-speed one-way traffic
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane one-way street design can encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk at the crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection corners to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and prioritize pedestrian movement.
